subject.title: [Feature]: Thread replies when agent uses tools; top-level for conversational responses

question: Should Slack add a default-off tool-use-sensitive reply-placement policy, and what precedence should it have relative to existing reply modes, per-channel overrides, DMs, existing threads, explicit top-level opt-outs, streaming, and status indicators?
rationale: The feature is absent and plausible, but it adds public config and changes user-visible reply routing, so automation should not choose the permanent policy shape.

options.title: Approve a precise Slack policy
options.body: Define the config shape and precedence, then implement the Slack-owned schema, routing, docs, and regression tests with default false for compatibility.

options.title: Use static reply controls only
options.body: Keep per-channel/account `replyToMode` as the supported channel-cleanliness control and close this request after maintainer confirmation.

options.title: Defer to broader channel policy
options.body: Hold this issue until maintainers design a shared reply-placement model with the overlapping Slack and Discord always-thread request.

recommendation.title: Approve a precise Slack policy
recommendation.body: Define the config shape and precedence, then implement the Slack-owned schema, routing, docs, and regression tests with default false for compatibility.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history across adjacent Slack reply-mode and threading decisions.
